I’ve just verified that the adapter install route expects a POST to /api/adapters/install with a JSON body containing at least a packageName (and optionally isLocalPath and version). The earlier inspection of the route code confirmed that it will accept a local filesystem path when isLocalPath is true, and it will read the package’s manifest to determine its version. 

My goal is to test the changes I made to the Groq adapter (adding the new tool “paperclip_get_comments” and updating the execution guidance). To ensure the running server picks up the patched code, I need to reload the adapter. The reload endpoint works, but it only reloads the currently installed version. Since I modified the source files directly in the r8 directory, the server may still be using a cached version from before the edits, and a simple reload might not reflect the new code if the version number hasn’t changed (the adapter store caches by version). 

A reliable way to force the server to load the new code is to create a fresh copy of the plugin with a bumped version string, then install that copy as a new adapter instance. The install route will treat it as a new version, write a fresh record, and load the code from that path. This avoids any caching issues and gives me a clean environment to verify the changes.

Steps:
1. Copy the entire r8 plugin directory to a new directory r9 under the same parent path. This preserves the modified files.
2. Update the version field in the new copy’s package.json from "0.7.0" to "0.7.1" so the server sees it as a distinct version.
3. Call the install API with packageName set to the absolute path of the new copy and isLocalPath=true, so the server knows to load from the filesystem rather than npm.
4. Capture a reasonable amount of the response (head -c 500) to confirm success without overwhelming the output.

All of these actions can be combined into a single Bash command: use `cp -r` for the copy, `sed -i` to edit the version, then `curl -s -X POST …` with the appropriate JSON payload. This command will be executed on the host where the Paperclip server is running, which matches the context of previous Bash calls.

Thus, the next appropriate tool call is a Bash execution that performs the copy, version bump, and install via the API.

arguments.command: cp -r /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/groq-paperclip-adapter-r8 /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/groq-paperclip-adapter-r9 && sed -i 's/"version": "0.7.0"/"version": "0.7.1"/' /home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/groq-paperclip-adapter-r9/package.json && curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3100/api/adapters/install -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"packageName":"/home/lane/.paperclip/adapter-plugins/groq-paperclip-adapter-r9","isLocalPath":true}' | head -c 500
arguments.description: Copy plugin to r9 and install via API
